gaps.text: ONE KERNEL in their bar: MatrixExponent.json has `enable_nanoda: false`.

The Lean model is DIVISION-FREE (gates: constant, input, add, sub, mul); the paper's Theorem 1.1 and its per-n bound allow division gates. A lower bound for division-free programs is weaker than one with divisions.
The per-n headline (⌈n^{9/4}/2⌉ gates at EVERY n ≥ 2) and Corollary 1.2 (geometric border rank of T_n ≥ n^{9/4}; asymptotic rank = n^{9/4}) are NOT in the challenge, which states exponents only.

The paper claims 1/2 ≤ α_F ≤ 2/3; the Lean states α = 1/2 and an exact rectangular formula, i.e. more than this paper claims; docs/107.md attributes the extra to three other manuscripts (two of 2026-09-24, one companion of 2026-11-24).

The literature as read disagrees on the upper bound: DeepMind's notebook of 2026-11-04 says "The current best bound is ω < 2.371339" and claims ω < 2.371177; the paper calls ω ≤ 9/4 known. The Lean, if it checks, proves both directions.
The build applies 28 compatibility patches to dependencies (lean/patches/); whether Mathlib or any patched dependency is in the closure of the three theorems is unmeasured.

`formalOmega` is an `sInf` of real numbers; Lean's `sInf` of an empty or unbounded-below set is 0. The control room's reading: the set is non-empty (schoolbook) and bounded below (N² degree-2 outputs) — to be PROVED (F3).
